jokes.punchline: 'What is more cuter-us than your uterus?' — a pun on 'cuter' and 'uterus' delivered with complete Leslie sincerity.
jokes.explanation: A perfect Leslie joke. The anatomical cartoon labeled 'Let's do this' is visual comedy inferred from context, and the pun 'cuter-us than your uterus' is exactly the kind of pun Leslie would coin — warm, slightly dorky, anatomically specific. 'The Knope way involves a lot of uterine cartoons' is also a great self-description. Highly quotable.

jokes.text: 'Let's make a baby together.' 'You should phrase that differently.' 'Right.'
jokes.setup: Leslie and Ann reconcile and agree to approach the sperm donor search together.
jokes.punchline: Leslie's declaration 'Let's make a baby together' sounds like a romantic proposition — Ann points this out, Leslie immediately agrees she should phrase it differently.
jokes.explanation: A clean callback to the Leslie-Ann romantic subtext. The joke is gentle and earned — Leslie says something that sounds intimate without meaning to, Ann flags it, Leslie acknowledges it immediately. Good economy and character integration. The predictability keeps it from scoring higher but the execution is clean.

jokes.text: Ben: 'Are you sure you're cool with JJ's Diner catering what you've referred to as "The wedding of the millennium"?' / Leslie: 'I thought that I could not love you any more than I already did. But I was dead wrong.'
jokes.setup: After the food poisoning disaster, Ben proposes JJ's Diner as the caterer — a humble local diner instead of an upscale caterer.
jokes.punchline: Leslie, who called this 'the wedding of the millennium,' finds JJ's Diner MORE romantic than fancy catering — revealing her priorities completely.
jokes.explanation: A warm character moment with comedic undertone. The fact that Leslie loves Ben more for choosing the humble local diner is exactly who she is — her love of Pawnee institutions overrides any aspiration to fanciness. 'I was dead wrong' about the limits of her love is a sweet-funny line.

jokes.text: Leslie and Ben smell smoke — something is burning.
jokes.setup: The romantic catering-resolution moment is happening; Leslie and Ben are having a warm scene.
jokes.punchline: Smoke. Something is literally on fire — cutting to April burning the pantsuit.
jokes.explanation: A well-constructed transitional joke. The smoke interrupting the warm moment is a classic sitcom scene-break device, but the payoff — April actually burning Leslie's pantsuit — gives it context-specific comedy.

jokes.text: April and Andy are burning Leslie's pantsuit in the parking lot. Leslie: 'That's mine. I wanted that back.' April: 'Well, frankly, you should have thought of that before we burned it.'
jokes.setup: Leslie finds April and Andy celebrating by burning a pantsuit.
jokes.punchline: April's response to Leslie's protest — 'you should have thought of that before we burned it' — is perfectly unapologetic and logically sound in the most unhelpful way possible.
jokes.explanation: A perfect episode-closing joke. 'You should have thought of that before we burned it' is a logically irrefutable but completely useless piece of advice — the kind of reasoning that's only 'correct' in the most technical sense. It's also the perfect payoff for April's hatred of the pantsuit established early in the episode. The 'frankly' adds a dignity to the absurdity. One of the episode's most quotable lines and a strong close.

jokes.text: Andy's confessional about April's forum success: 'She was awesome. So smart, so hot, so mean. I wanted to bone her right there in that dirty church basement.'
jokes.setup: Andy reports on April's successful forum performance.
jokes.punchline: His admiration escalates from compliments ('smart, hot, mean') to announcing he wanted to have sex with her in a church basement — delivered with complete guileless sincerity.
jokes.explanation: Classic Andy confessional humor. His earnest list of compliments — 'smart, hot, mean' — followed by the church basement declaration is oversharing at its finest. Andy has no filter between admiration and carnal expression, and the specific venue ('dirty church basement') makes it funnier. The 'meant as a compliment' energy is pure Andy.

tmdb_overview: Ann tries to get to know herself as Leslie meddles in one of her biggest life decisions. Meanwhile, things go south when Ben enlists the guys to help choose a caterer for the wedding.
insight: Emotional episode softens comedy load—68 jokes still land via character depth over punchline density.
